title: Universal Tensor Squares for Symmetric Groups
main_claim: For every n other than 2, 4 and 9, there is a self-conjugate partition λ of n such that the Kronecker coefficient g(λ,λ,ν) is positive for every ν ⊢ n. This would settle the Pak–Panova–Vallejo tensor square conjecture. For M ≥ 9 the proof uses an explicit candidate L: a staircase with matched additions to its first two rows and columns. It combines (i) a band criterion, which is a triangle quotient that applies the companion cyclic Saxl theorem, together with an odd-path contraction and two symmetric-form attachments, and (ii) balance tests that separate components by output size and sum. Area/capacity inequalities and 19 exceptional (M,r) pairs, closed by computer, finish the large case. Degrees n ≤ 64 are handled by exact Murnaghan–Nakayama character residues mod 1e9+7 and 1e9+9.

issues.description: The whole result depends on the companion paper 'A Cyclic Polytabloid Proof of Saxl's Conjecture', Thm 3.1. That theorem says every irreducible occurs in the specific cyclic row/column module W_m, which is stronger than Saxl's conjecture, itself a well-known open problem. This is a dependency, not an error. The cited statement and conventions (B_m, ordered rows and columns, the alphabet e_1..e_m) match the companion's Theorem thm:cyclic-saxl exactly, and there is no circularity: the companion does not use this paper. The companion's proof was not audited here.
issues.evidence: Compared the companion's build/sections/dominance.tex (eq. dom:cyclic-module, Theorem thm:cyclic-saxl) with this paper's eq. cyclic-generator. They match, including that the relabeling of the marked alphabet in the triangle quotient preserves order.

coverage: Checked by hand: Lemma candidate (parity/r bounds; size and self-conjugacy also checked by script for 65 ≤ n < 3000); sector induction; triangle quotient (marked-letter counts per row and column, uniqueness of the margins forcing A=D, the factorization into w_{M-2}⊗u_F, the branching step); the decomposition of F into the path and E_±, and which blocks are extended; the separated contraction; the odd-path lemma (matrix formula and the existence of a nonvanishing basis, verified numerically for k=1..9 over all compositions with parts ≤4); one-extra (H-alternating line, multiplicity one, contractions with an orthonormal form); two-extras (LR splits, κ self-complement, size and parity bookkeeping); the no-cancellation argument in the proof of the band criterion (flag ordering, chosen columns kept away from the extended blocks, positions ≥5 and ≤K-4); balance separation by output count and sum; the neighboring and two-path labelings and their output ranges; removal of the horizontal 2-strip; the odd-strip interval; the packing bounds |A| ≥ 2M-5 and max A ≤ M+1 and the dominance verification; the three-row density map (determinant lemma, rank-2 symmetric decomposition, Zariski density, Pieri/Schur–Weyl); the rectangle lemma; the polynomial inequalities in Lemma capacity-large; derivation of the D-set; soundness of the hit/bound/prune lemmas; the MN recurrence weights. Reran: capacity_checks intermediate (PASS) and exceptional (PASS, about 347 s); smallcode for n=10, 30, 50, 64 (exit 0; n=64 took 157 s when run alone). I did not rerun all 61 degrees or the independent comparison harness, did not line-audit the C++ and Python sources against the text, and did not audit the companion Saxl paper.
